target.title: Fix Gemini helper timeout reliability
target.body:
## Summary

- Make synchronous Gemini package-discovery waits independent of termination-handler callbacks and stale `Process.isRunning` state.
- Observe child completion on a dedicated thread while preserving the bounded deadline and hard process-group termination for stuck helpers.
- Close the parent's duplicated pipe writers, return after the first complete output line, and resolve the fixture/user `fnm` from the effective environment path.
- Cover delayed success, first-line extraction, prompt no-output failure, inherited pipe writers, environment-path resolution, and ignored-SIGTERM escalation.
- Preserve five minutes of macOS shard headroom for the repository's observed 35-minute test-step boundary.
- Document the user-visible reliability fix in the changelog.

## Proof

- `swift test --filter GeminiStatusProbeAPITests` — 19 tests passed, then repeated five more times with `--skip-build`; all six runs passed on the repaired implementation.
- `make check` — repository guards, 145 documentation links, 22 site locales, SwiftFormat, and SwiftLint passed; 0 violations across 1,246 linted files.
- `make test` — all 46 sharded groups passed on the repaired current-main candidate; the harness's configured one-time retry was exercised for shard 15.
- Freshly built CLI live proof — `CodexBarCLI usage --provider gemini --format json` exited 0 and returned one Gemini provider record with usage and no error; identity values were not printed.
- Installed helper proof — `fnm current` returned `v25.8.1`, and `fnm exec --using v25.8.1 npm root -g` returned the active global package root.
- Autoreview — clean, no accepted/actionable findings (0.82 confidence).

## Risk

Low. The runtime change is provider-scoped; the helper remains synchronous and bounded, escalates to hard process-group termination after the deadline, and now has direct success and failure-path coverage. The CI-only change adds timeout headroom without changing test selection or pass criteria.
